findings.title: A skip-ci landing route is labelled as reviewed under doc 79, and [skip ci] is already in the payload commit message
findings.claim: The payload record labels skipMechanism 'PROPOSED_DOC79_REVIEWED_SKIP_CI_ROUTE_NOT_SELECTED_OR_PUBLISHED' and destination 'VIA_REVIEWED_WORKFLOW_ONLY_ROUTE'. The landing observation refers to an 'explicitly selected reviewed skip-CI landing route'. Doc 79 reviewed no skip-ci route. Its CI-5 accepted only the PR-then-merge route, which triggers main's three jobs, and proposal r2 says skip-ci is 'not selected, does not suppress all triggers'. The payload commit (parented directly on main, message ending in [skip ci]) produces different automatic runs depending on the landing method. Per docs, skip applies only to push and pull_request, and for a PR only when it is in the HEAD commit. So a PR whose head carries [skip ci] skips its pull_request runs; a merge commit without the string still runs on the main push; a rebase or fast-forward keeps the skip; and a direct push is r2's retained alternative, which needs its own exact approval. Non-Actions consumers are not affected by skip. The records do not determine which automatic runs will occur.

findings.title: Successful-run export hard-links container-owned files; PASS unreachable under protected_hardlinks
findings.claim: When every test passes, collect() hard-links every OUT file into EXPORT. Several of those files were written by container UID 1000 with mode 0644, and the runner user is non-root. With Linux fs.protected_hardlinks=1, the Ubuntu and systemd default, a user may not hard-link a file it does not own unless it has read and write access. os.link therefore fails with EPERM. The failure is caught as CONTROLLER_UNKNOWN_PermissionError and becomes the first recorded cause, which triggers the emergency metadata-only artifact, and finalize records FAILED_OR_INCOMPLETE. The single attempt is consumed even though all three tests passed. Nothing in the bytes ever produces SYNTHETIC_SUBSET_PASS on a default-configured runner.

The observer writes observer-<pid>.json and unhandled-<pid> with mode 0o644 (:140, :142, :149). The wrapper writes child.exit (:591), and Vitest writes .ci-pilot/out/<label>.json (:745), both in phase_out (:556). The inventory covers every OUT file (:789-801). On the non-metadata path, os.link(OUT/item['path'], dest) (:815-819). The non-root design is implied by sudo -n du/chown (:295, :713), and the author's comment at :555 notes the cross-UID writes. Reasoned from kernel link-restriction semantics. findings.title: The resource watcher refuses whenever du sees a file vanish during the scan
findings.claim: All control commands accept only exit 0. GNU du exits nonzero when an entry it listed disappears before it can stat it, reporting "cannot access". The watcher runs sudo du over the npm cache, node_modules and the whole Docker root roughly every second, during the image pull and npm ci. Those are exactly the windows where temp files are created and renamed: npm cache tmp entries, Docker tmp blobs and layer write-sets. One such race writes CONTROL_COMMAND_FAILED as the first cause and the watcher refuses. execute then aborts with PRIOR_FAILURE and the attempt is consumed with no test result. This is a plausible, intermittent self-refusal, not a resource breach.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39. small() accepts only allowed=(0,) and requires returncode in allowed (:255, :278). resources() runs sudo -n du -sx -B1 -- on each role (:295) over [SRC], [DockerRootDir], [DEPS, CACHE] and the evidence paths (:285-287). The watcher calls resources on every loop with a 0.5 s sleep (:418-431). Any exception means refuse plus stopping own containers (:432-442). healthy() refuses on an existing failure record (:446). Reasoned from GNU du and fts error semantics. NOT RUN; how often the race occurs is NOT MEASURED.
findings.fix: Treat transient vanished-entry errors as retryable within the existing per-command time bound: re-run du a bounded number of times and refuse only on persistent failure or on errors other than vanished files. Alternatively, keep known temp directories out of the role du while device free space still covers them. Record the retries in telemetry.

findings.title: The image disk role measures DockerRootDir only; under the containerd store, image bytes are not counted
findings.claim: The image role is measured as du of info['DockerRootDir'] and nothing else. docs.docker.com says the containerd image store is the default for Docker Engine 29.0 and later on fresh installations. It also says containerd uses a separate storage path from the Docker data directory and stores images both compressed and uncompressed. The workflow never checks the storage driver or DriverStatus. On such a runner the 2 GiB image cap is therefore not enforced and the receipt understates image use. CI-7 requires that if ownership or accounting cannot be bounded, the run refuses; here it silently under-measures instead. The device-level free-space check stays conservative, so this is an evidence and role-cap defect, not a disk-exhaustion risk.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39. The image role is ('imageLayersExpansion', [Path(s['dockerRoot'])], 2*GiB) (:285). dockerRoot comes from DockerRootDir (:395, :399). docker info is checked only for CgroupVersion and OSType (:393-394), and state.provider records ServerVersion but not Driver or DriverStatus (:400-404). CI-7 in revision 2 (e01f8ea CI_PILOT_PROPOSAL_20261009.md) says to count shared image and layer use conservatively and to refuse if ownership or accounting cannot be bounded. The runner's Docker version and storage mode are NOT OBSERVED.

Either require the legacy graph driver and refuse otherwise, or detect driver-type io.containerd.snapshotter.v1 and include containerd's actual root in the image role, keeping the same-device rule, else refuse. findings.title: ImageVersion must equal a literal bound before dispatch, but it only exists after job assignment
findings.claim: Admission requires os.environ['ImageVersion'] to equal BIND['runner_image_version'], and BIND has to be landed in a reviewed successor before dispatch. The runner image version belongs to whichever machine is assigned after the dispatch event, so its controlling stage is post-dispatch. The supplemental provider record says this fact cannot be replaced by current release metadata. A truthful pre-dispatch binding is therefore impossible: either a guess is bound, against 'NOT ... inferred facts' (:71), or a mismatch refuses with RUNNER_IMAGE and consumes the attempt. ImageVersion is also not among the default variables documented on docs.github.com.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 :346 require(os.environ.get('ImageVersion') == BIND['runner_image_version'], 'RUNNER_IMAGE'). BIND is to be filled in a reviewed successor and is not a dispatch input (:70-72, :81). The attempt is consumed on refusal (:178, :331). The value is already recorded as an observation (:400). Registration supplementalActualProviderFacts records actualFutureRunnerImageVersion NOT_OBSERVED and lists 'Future actual runner/ImageVersion/admission measurements not replaceable by current release metadata'. The docs.github.com variables reference lists GITHUB_* and RUNNER_* variables only.
findings.fix: Gate only on facts that can be bound before dispatch: RUNNER_OS and RUNNER_ARCH, and ImageOS if it is accepted. Keep ImageVersion as a recorded observation (:400). Otherwise Samuel should explicitly accept that an image-version mismatch consumes the attempt. Do not bind a guessed literal.

findings.title: Two full node_modules hashes, with a health check per entry, sit inside the shared 60 s preflight budget
findings.claim: Admission, source preflight, installed evidence, three validations and final integrity all draw on one cumulative 60 s preflight allowance. Two of those phases run manifest() over the whole installed tree. manifest() calls healthy() for every entry, and each call re-reads and parses state.json and telemetry.json and reads two /proc files. With 672 lock entries, including lucide-react 0.545.0, date-fns 3.6.0 and typescript 5.6.3, that is plausibly tens of thousands of entries. An overrun refuses with PHASE_DEADLINE_* and consumes the attempt, possibly after tests have passed. The fix is to the implementation; no selected threshold has to change.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39. The preflight cap is cumulative: seconds = min(seconds, 60-used['preflight']) (:239). Phases: admission (:352), source-runtime-preflight (:705), installed-evidence with manifest (:732-738), validate-* (:747-748), final-source-integrity with manifest (:749-752). healthy() runs per rglob entry (:649-650). healthy() reads state, telemetry and /proc (:445-451). Phase deadline at :228. git show 1631323:package-lock.json has 672 node_modules entries. Entry count and timing are NOT MEASURED.
findings.fix: Call healthy() at a bounded interval during manifest, for example every N entries or every 0.5 s, instead of once per entry, and record how long each manifest took. If the 60 s bucket is kept, the decision text should say that it includes two full installed-tree hashes.

findings.title: Step-level timeouts add an unselected ceiling below the execution allocations
findings.claim: The step timeouts total exactly 30 minutes. The execution step's 21 minutes (1260 s) is shorter than the allocations that fall inside it: up to 60 + 365 + 305 + 3x185 = 1285 s, plus transitions. The step timeout can therefore kill the controller before its own phase deadlines. The outcome is still fail-closed, because a step timeout is not a cancellation and collection runs under !cancelled(). In-step cleanup of named containers then depends on the SIGINT to KeyboardInterrupt path (SIGINT, 7.5 s, SIGTERM, 2.5 s, kill tree).
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 step timeouts at :50 (1), :931 (2), :944 (21), :949 (3), :957 (2), :968 (1). Allocations at :720, :592, :746. docs.github.com: a step timeout is the maximum minutes to run the step before killing the process, and job timeout-minutes means GitHub automatically cancels the job. The workflow-cancellation reference gives the SIGINT/SIGTERM sequence.
findings.fix: Treat step timeouts as backstops set at or above the controller's allocations, keeping job timeout-minutes: 30 as the outer bound (step values need not add up to 30). Otherwise name the 21-minute step timeout as an additional selected ceiling.

findings.title: memory.events 'max' > 0 is refused even without an OOM
findings.claim: run_container refuses when memory.events max, oom or oom_kill is nonzero. In cgroup v2, max counts the times usage reached the limit and the kernel reclaimed, including page cache charged to the cgroup; it does not mean an OOM occurred. The install container, writing node_modules and the npm cache under a 2 GiB cap, is the plausible trigger. The adopted choice is a 2 GiB ceiling, and W-2 asks to record exit and OOM state. Refusing on any contact with the limit is stricter than that and can consume the attempt with no OOM.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 :615 require(all(sample['memoryEvents'].get(k,0) == 0 for k in ['max','oom','oom_kill']), 'MEMORY_LIMIT_REFUSAL'). memory.events is read at :511. doc79 W-2 and doc77 CI-12 cover PIDs and OOM recording only. Reasoned from cgroup v2 semantics; docs.docker.com does not say whether page cache counts. NOT RUN.
findings.fix: Record max, and refuse on oom, oom_kill or OOMKilled. Otherwise put the cap-contact refusal explicitly in the decision text, since it consumes the attempt.

findings.title: Isolation flags are not checked after create, and the npm cache stays writable in test containers
findings.claim: Post-create inspection checks memory, swap, PIDs, CPU, user and read-only root, but not NetworkMode (none for tests), CapDrop ALL, no-new-privileges, the read/write flags of each mount, tmpfs or the log driver. The receipt keeps only the requested argv. Separately, /ci-cache is bind-mounted writable into all three test containers, although the tests need only node_modules (for .vite-temp) and the output mount. Revision 2 specifies writable dependencies and output for tests.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 inspection at :602-606. The requested options are stored in the receipt (:594). The cache bind at :585 applies to every run_container call, tests included (:746). Revision 2 text: 'Tests use --network none ... read-only root and tracked source, dedicated writable dependencies/output'.
findings.fix: Require HostConfig.NetworkMode == 'none' for tests, CapDrop == ['ALL'], no-new-privileges in SecurityOpt, the expected RW/RO flag on each mount, and the exact tmpfs and log driver. Omit the cache mount from test containers or make it readonly.

findings.title: The worker heap check would also pass if 1024 MiB were never applied
findings.claim: heap_size_limit only has to be between 0 and 1152 MiB. With --max-old-space-size=1024 in effect, heap_size_limit is at least 1024 MiB. A worker where the setting did not take effect would get a default sized from the 2 GiB cgroup, plausibly below 1024 MiB, and would still pass. Today the heap statistic does not corroborate the selected 1024 MiB; only the NODE_OPTIONS string comparison does.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 :698 require(0 < worker['heap']['heap_size_limit'] < 1152*MiB). Env string equality is at :692. Revision 2 CI-2 asks for worker V8 heap statistics as evidence.
findings.fix: Use a lower bound of 1024 MiB (heap_size_limit >= 1024*MiB) while keeping the 1152 MiB upper bound and the existing comment that total heap is not exactly 1024 MiB.

findings.title: Ordinary failures drop complete, in-limit raw evidence; the stream complete flag and hidden-file handling are imprecise
findings.claim: Any failure makes the artifact metadata-only. Its diagnostics include only top-level OUT/*.json files of at most 64 KiB. The per-file Vitest JSON under OUT/<label>/ and the fully drained, in-limit child streams are left out, so with a single attempt a test failure would leave only a reason code. Stream complete=outcome is None marks fully drained streams as incomplete on any failure. Upload include-hidden-files: false could drop a dotfile listed in receipt.json without the receipt showing that. The records disclose that failed raw data stays on the ephemeral runner, so this is about diagnosability, not a breach of a rule.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 metadata_only on any failure (:810). Diagnostics glob and size limits (:824-826). The complete flag (:636). include-hidden-files: false (:964). Records f76c2fb3 limitations: 'failed raw data stay on ephemeral runner'.
findings.fix: For ordinary failures within limits, export the complete bounded files, keeping metadata-only for overflow and unknown states. Set completeness from drain or EOF state, not from success. Either set include-hidden-files: true or refuse when OUT contains hidden files.

findings.title: Tight docker CLI bounds and undocumented name-filter anchors can mark a passing run unqualified
findings.claim: Each docker inspect, rm and ps in finish_container is bounded at 0.5 s, docker run --detach and du at 3 s. One slow CLI call on a passing run gives CONTAINER_CLEANUP_UNKNOWN and then CONTAINER_NOT_QUALIFIED. The worst-case sum of those bounds on the stop/kill path, about 6.2 s, exceeds the 5 s grace. The exact-name filter name=^/<name>$ relies on regex and leading-slash behaviour that docs.docker.com does not document; it says only that the filter matches on all or part of a container's name. If the anchors were not honoured, collection would skip inspecting and removing a leftover container, and the label check would refuse with no exit or OOM record. That path is fail-closed, but the evidence is lost.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 per-call bounds at :522-538, run at :598, du at :295, grace at :632, refusal at :640-641. Name filters at :538 and :776, label check at :781. docs.docker.com container ls: 'The name filter matches on all or part of a container's name.'
findings.fix: Find run containers by --filter label=xenios-ci-pilot=<RUN> and compare --format {{.Names}} for exact equality. Replace the fixed 0.5 s per-call bounds with one remaining-grace budget for the whole sequence.

findings.title: Anonymous Docker Hub pull and digest availability are unbound provider facts
findings.claim: DOCKER_CONFIG is set to an empty auths file, so the pull is anonymous. docs.docker.com limits unauthenticated pulls to 100 per 6 hours per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 and documents no exemption for hosted runners. The assigned runner's egress IP and whether the digest is still available cannot be observed in advance, and a pull failure consumes the attempt. W-3 avoids that consumption for the source commit; there is no counterpart check for the image digest.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 empty auths and DOCKER_CONFIG (:390-392, :911), pull at :721, captured-command refusal at :489. docs.docker.com docker-hub/usage.
findings.fix: Add a W-3-style read-only check, immediately before dispatch, that the digest manifest can be retrieved. Name the shared-egress rate limit in the decision record as an accepted, unbound risk.

findings.title: The ACTIONS_*_DEBUG='false' job env values do not control provider debug logging
findings.claim: The job env sets ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG and ACTIONS_RUNNER_DEBUG to 'false'. docs.github.com says debug logging is turned on through a repository secret or variable, and that anyone who can run the workflow can enable it on a re-run; it does not document workflow env as a control. A debug re-run is refused only inside the admission step, after set-up and step debug output has started. The runner also echoes the full inline controller into the provider log. These are provider-log facts that belong under the UNBOUND barrier, not filtering the bytes achieve.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml@e86ffe39 :45-46. Attempt guard at :340. Barrier at :85-89 and :341. docs.github.com enable-debug-logging. The supplemental observation recorded 0 repository variables and 0 secrets at one point in time.
findings.fix: Label these env lines as non-controlling. Keep provider-log control under the UNBOUND receipt, and record the repository debug variable and secret absence observation at the controlling stage, next to the window.

No interpreter, docker, npm, test, checkout, commit, fetch, push, PR or session contact.

The runner's sysctl, kernel pids.peak, Docker version and storage mode, ImageVersion, capacity and timings are NOT OBSERVED. The entry counts and timings in W2-2 and W2-5 are estimates, not measurements.

verdicts.note: Upheld. Two conditions apply. (1) The runner UID must differ from container UID 1000. docs.github.com names no runner user. Hosted Ubuntu images commonly run as uid 1001, but this is NOT OBSERVED, and if the runner were uid 1000 the link would succeed. (2) fs.protected_hardlinks must be 1, which is the Ubuntu and systemd default; NOT OBSERVED. Under these conditions may_linkat requires ownership, read+write access or CAP_FOWNER. Container files are 0644: observer and unhandled files are written with mode 0o644 (:140, :142, :149); child.exit and the Vitest JSON get 0666&~022 (:591, :745). Even install/child.exit is container-written. The first sorted inventory item, admin-readback/admin-readback.json, fails at os.link (:819). The recorded first cause is CONTROLLER_UNKNOWN_PermissionError via the main handler, followed by emergency metadata-only and FAILED_OR_INCOMPLETE. This is fail-closed, not a silent pass, but no SYNTHETIC_SUBSET_PASS is reachable. Another fix option: a wrapper `umask 000` applied only to phase_out writes, or recorded `sudo -n chmod a+rw` on the exact inventory files before linking. Either keeps the hard-link dedupe inside the 32 MiB evidence role.

Upheld and strengthened. Besides the npm cacache tmp entries and the pull tmp blobs, the bytes themselves create entries that vanish inside du-scanned roles: (a) each of the four `docker rm` calls (:537) deletes containers/<id>, overlay2/<id> and <id>-init while the watcher may be running du over DockerRootDir (:285, :295); (b) dockerd atomically rewrites config.v2.json and hostconfig.json in containers/<id> on every start and stop; (c) Vite 7.3.5 (lock@1631323) bundles vitest.config.ts to a timestamped file in node_modules/.vite-temp and unlinks it at each test start, inside the DEPS role; (d) the controller's own state.json.<pid>.tmp and telemetry.json.<pid>.tmp (:168) sit in CONTROL, which is part of the evidenceStreams role (:287), and main-process resources() calls run concurrently with the watcher's telemetry writes (:424). Per-event probability is low to moderate and NOT MEASURED, but there are many events and any one refuses (:278). P2 is kept.

Upheld. The image role is du of DockerRootDir only (:285, :395-399). Driver and DriverStatus are neither checked nor recorded (:393-404). Under the containerd snapshotter, image content and snapshots live outside DockerRootDir, so the 2 GiB role cap is unenforced. Revision-2 CI-7 (e01f8ea proposal :116) requires refusal when accounting cannot be bounded. The device-level free-space check still holds, so this is a cap and evidence defect, not a disk-exhaustion risk. The runner's Docker version and store are NOT OBSERVED.

Upheld, with the rationale refined. ImageVersion is a runner-images environment variable present on hosted images; its absence from the docs.github.com default-variable list is not the core issue. The core issue is that the dispatcher cannot choose which image version is assigned, and images roll out progressively over days. A bound literal at :346 is therefore a selected requirement whose mismatch is outside anyone's control and consumes the attempt (:178, :331). It is also stricter than the adopted 'ubuntu-24.04'. The fix stands: gate on RUNNER_OS/RUNNER_ARCH (and ImageOS if accepted), and keep ImageVersion as the observation already recorded at :400.

Upheld, with the uncertainty stated. healthy() runs for every rglob entry, directories included, before the S_ISDIR skip (:649-650, :661). Each call parses state.json and telemetry.json and reads two /proc files (:445-451). For a 672-entry tree my rough estimate is about 50k-120k entries at roughly 0.1-0.3 ms each, i.e. about 10-20 s per manifest. Two manifests plus admission, preflight and three validations share one 60 s bucket (:239), which is tight but not certainly over. Timing is NOT MEASURED. The fix (throttle healthy() during manifest) is cheap, so P2 is kept.

Upheld. The step timeouts at :50, :931, :944, :949, :957 and :968 sum to exactly 30 minutes. The 21-minute execution step (1260 s) is shorter than the 365+305+3x185 s allocations plus the remaining preflight. A step-timeout kill is still fail-closed, because collection runs under !cancelled() and the runner sends SIGINT, then SIGTERM after 7.5 s. Python has no SIGTERM handler, so finish_container can be cut short and collection then removes leftovers by name.

Upheld. In cgroup v2, the 'max' counter increments on reclaim at memory.max even when no OOM occurs. Page cache from npm ci writing node_modules and the cache through bind mounts is charged to the container cgroup, so an install footprint near 2 GiB would refuse at :615 without an OOM. The footprint is NOT MEASURED. If a measured install approaches the cap, this should rise to P2.

Upheld. Post-create inspection (:602-606) omits NetworkMode, CapDrop, SecurityOpt, the RO/RW flag of each mount, tmpfs and log driver. /ci-cache (:585) is writable in all test containers. Revision-2 :124 lists dependencies and output as the writable mounts for tests, although CI-9's authored control names the cache path, so this is an author condition.

Upheld. Reasoned, NOT RUN: with --max-old-space-size=1024, V8 11.3 on 64-bit without pointer compression gives heap_size_limit of about 1024 + 24 MiB of young generation, roughly 1048 MiB. The proposed lower bound of 1024 MiB with the 1152 MiB upper bound therefore holds for a correct run and would reject a cgroup-sized default.

Upheld. In the metadata-only path, diagnostics glob only top-level OUT/*.json files of at most 64 KiB (:824-826). Per-label Vitest JSON in OUT/<label>/ is never included, so a test failure leaves only receipts. complete=outcome is None (:636) conflates drain state with success. The records disclose that failed raw data stays on the runner.

Upheld, with one correction. A per-call timeout inside small() calls require, and therefore refuse('CONTROL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT') (:265). That writes the immutable first cause, so the recorded cause is CONTROL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT (or TERMINATION_GRACE_EXPIRED from bounded()), not CONTAINER_CLEANUP_UNKNOWN. small() also SIGKILLs the docker CLI while the daemon continues the rm. The worst-case bound sum exceeding the 5 s grace is confirmed.

Upheld. Pulls are anonymous: DOCKER_CONFIG points at empty auths (:390-392). Docker Hub's per-IP limits and whether the digest is still available are unbound provider facts. A pull failure consumes the attempt, and there is no W-3-style pre-dispatch digest check.

Upheld. ACTIONS_*_DEBUG='false' in job env (:45-46) does not override a repository secret or variable, or a debug re-run. upheld.title: The success-path export hard-links files owned by container UID 1000, so a passing run cannot reach PASS
upheld.claim:
collect() takes the non-metadata path only when no failure exists and the payload is at most 18 MiB. On that path it runs os.link for every OUT file into EXPORT (:815-819). OUT/<label>/ contains files written inside the containers under --user 1000:1000 (:579), all mode 0644:
- child.exit (:591)
- the Vitest JSON (:745)
- observer-*.json (:140)
- install/child.exit

The bytes themselves assume the runner UID is not 1000: see the sudo chown 1000:1000 at :713 and the dual-UID comment at :554-555. With fs.protected_hardlinks=1 (the Ubuntu/systemd default), a non-owner without CAP_FOWNER can hard-link a file only if it can both read and write it. Mode 0644 gives group and other read only, so the link fails with EPERM.

The first sorted item, admin-readback/admin-readback.json, raises PermissionError. The main handler then records CONTROLLER_UNKNOWN_PermissionError as the first cause and runs emergency metadata-only collection, and finalize writes FAILED_OR_INCOMPLETE (:891-893).

This fails closed, but a run where all three tests pass still consumes the attempt, and SYNTHETIC_SUBSET_PASS is unreachable. Two conditions are NOT OBSERVED: the runner UID must differ from 1000 (hosted images commonly use 1001), and protected_hardlinks must be 1.
upheld.fix:
In the successor, make the export independent of cross-UID hard links. Options:
(a) A recorded `sudo -n chown` of exactly the inventoried OUT files to the runner UID before linking (the sudo path is already used at :295 and :713).
(b) A wrapper umask that makes phase_out writes read-write for the runner.
(c) Upload OUT plus a separate receipt directly.

If files are copied instead, revisit the 32 MiB evidence role, since 18 MiB OUT plus 18 MiB EXPORT exceeds it. Also confirm that manifest() can read every npm-written dependency file as the runner user.

upheld.title: The only recorded main payload carries the UNBOUND blob, and the landing order and count are left open (merges W1-1, W1V-6, W2V-4)
upheld.claim:
Commit 3bb4afda (parent 6077a6bb) lands blob 2d40bd2a. Every BIND literal in that blob is UNBOUND, so every accepted event first takes run_number 1 (:340) and then refuses at :341. Line :11 and authority line 105 ('Do not create a second filename variant') forbid regaining run_number 1. Binding the values changes the blob, so 3bb4afda can never be the dispatched bytes. Even so, the records present it as the prospective main payload and do not say whether landing happens once (the bound successor only) or twice.

The bytes also require execution-stage facts inside the landed blob: dispatcher, window, reservation and execution receipt (:72-86, :342-345). Doc 77 section 4 steps 7/9 and doc 79 section 4 steps 5-6 instead place landing before execution approval. The bytes therefore reverse that order and tie the landing date to the window. A landing that slips past not_after leaves dead bytes on main while the D-2 trigger stays live.
upheld.fix:
Record that 3bb4afda/2d40bd2a must never land. The only landable payload is the compared, fully bound successor, landed once on the then-current main with its own route and automatic-run inventory.

Record the corrected sequence:
1. Compare 2d40bd2a.
2. Bind typed values.
3. Compare the successor.
4. Land once.
5. Run the W-1 blob/parent check.
6. Dispatch once inside the window.

Choose not_before only after landing and the W-1 check can complete. State that a missed window requires a new successor and a new landing route.

upheld.title: A skip-ci landing route is attributed to doc 79 review, and the automatic runs of landing are undetermined (W1-2)
upheld.claim:
The payload labels its skipMechanism 'PROPOSED_DOC79_REVIEWED_SKIP_CI_ROUTE' and its destination 'VIA_REVIEWED_WORKFLOW_ONLY_ROUTE'. Its commit message is 'ci: add bounded manual Quick Order pilot [skip ci]'.

Doc 79 reviewed no skip-ci route. 'skip' appears only as the test-status word at :55, and :54 (CI-5) accepted PR-then-merge, which runs main's jobs. Proposal r2 :86 says skip-ci 'is not selected, does not suppress all triggers'.

checks.yml at 6077a6bb triggers on pull_request and on push to main: npm ci with lifecycle scripts, full Vitest, typecheck and build. Skip applies only to push and pull_request, and for a PR only via its HEAD commit. So the runs that actually fire depend on the merge method and on the final merge-commit message, which can carry the PR title. Main is unprotected (:8). Non-Actions consumers, such as GitHub App installations including the Render integration, are not suppressed by skip-ci.
upheld.fix:
Remove the doc 79 attribution and record skip-ci as unreviewed. Select one landing route, recording the merge method and the final commit message. List its exact automatic Actions runs and its non-Actions consumers.

Any route whose automatic runs are not covered goes to the single 'ask about that exact effect once' decision (authority lines 152-153). It also needs review if it differs from the PR-then-merge route that doc 79 checked.

upheld.title: The gating unauthenticated jobs-API read (3 s timeout) can burn the attempt on provider rate limits or latency (merges W1-4, W2V-1, timeout part of W1V-1)
upheld.claim:
Admission requires an unauthenticated GET to api.github.com with timeout=3, no retry and no handler (:356-366). This happens after run_number 1 is taken (:340) and before checkout.

Per docs.github.com, unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 per hour per originating IP, and exceeding the limit returns 403 or 429. Any HTTPError, URLError, 5xx or timeout becomes CONTROLLER_UNKNOWN_* (:913-918) and consumes the only attempt. The egress IP and quota of a hosted runner cannot be observed before dispatch. The records name only private, unavailable or ambiguous responses as refusal causes.

Severity is resolved to P2 (W1 and its verifier said P3, the W2 verifier said P2). The gate is in the bytes, it permanently consumes the pilot, and a correction can be made in the bytes.
upheld.fix:
Choose one option in the successor and record it:
(a) Make the provider job start a recorded, non-gating observation. When it is unavailable, use the Runner.Worker origin minus a fixed recorded margin.
(b) Authenticate only this read. That changes token exposure and needs its own decision.
(c) Samuel explicitly accepts this attempt-consuming refusal in the window decision.

Do not add retries that can exceed the 60 s preflight bucket.

upheld.title: Exact ImageVersion equality requires a value that only exists after job assignment (merges W1-3, W2-4)
upheld.claim:
:346 requires the ImageVersion environment variable to equal a literal landed before dispatch. The image version is fixed only when a machine is assigned after the event. Images roll out progressively, and the dispatcher cannot choose a version. The registration records actualFutureRunnerImageVersion NOT_OBSERVED and calls it 'not replaceable by current release metadata'.

A truthful pre-dispatch binding is therefore impossible. Either a guess is bound, contrary to :71 ('NOT ... inferred facts'), or a mismatch refuses with RUNNER_IMAGE and permanently consumes run_number 1. The gate is also stricter than the adopted ubuntu-24.04 label.

Severity is resolved to P2 (the W1 lens said P3).
upheld.fix: Remove the equality gate. Keep ImageVersion as the observation already recorded at :400. Gate only on RUNNER_OS and RUNNER_ARCH, plus ImageOS if accepted. Alternatively, Samuel explicitly accepts the mismatch as a cause that consumes the attempt. Never bind a guessed literal.

upheld.title: The watcher refuses whenever du sees an entry vanish mid-scan (W2-2)
upheld.claim:
small() accepts only exit 0 (:255, :278). The watcher runs `sudo -n du -sx` over the checkout, the whole DockerRootDir, DEPS+CACHE and the evidence paths on every loop (:418-431). GNU du exits nonzero when a listed entry disappears before it is visited. The bytes create such races themselves:
- Each `docker rm` (:537) deletes containers/<id> and overlay2/<id>/<id>-init while du may be partway through overlay2.
- Image pulls remove temporary blobs.
- The npm cacache tmp directory moves entries.
- The controller writes its own *.<pid>.tmp files inside CONTROL (:168), which is part of the evidence role.
- Vite unlinks .vite-temp bundles inside DEPS.

Any one race writes CONTROL_COMMAND_FAILED as the first cause, and the attempt is consumed with no test result. The frequency is NOT MEASURED; there are many events, and any single one refuses.
upheld.fix: Treat vanished-entry du errors as retryable within the existing per-command bound, and refuse only on persistent failures or on other errors. Alternatively, keep known temp directories out of role du while device free space still covers them. Record the retries in telemetry.

upheld.title: The image disk role measures only DockerRootDir and is blind under the containerd image store (W2-3)
upheld.claim:
The image role is du of DockerRootDir only. docker info is checked for CgroupVersion and OSType, and Driver and DriverStatus are neither checked nor recorded. Per docs.docker.com, the containerd image store is the default for fresh Docker Engine 29+ installs and keeps image content outside the Docker data directory. On such a runner the 2 GiB image cap is unenforced and the receipt under-reports. That contradicts r2 CI-7, which says to refuse when accounting cannot be bounded.

The device-level free-space check remains conservative, so this is a cap and evidence defect, not a disk-exhaustion risk. The runner's Docker version and store are NOT OBSERVED.
upheld.fix: Bind the storage mode from docker info. Either require the legacy graph driver and refuse otherwise, or detect the containerd snapshotter and include its actual root in the image role, keeping the same-device rule. Record Driver and DriverStatus in state.provider.

upheld.title: Two full node_modules manifests, with healthy() called per entry, share the 60 s preflight bucket (W2-5)
upheld.claim:
manifest() calls healthy() for every rglob entry, directories included, before the S_ISDIR skip (:649-650). Each healthy() call:
- re-reads and parses state.json and telemetry.json
- reads two /proc files
- runs check_time, which enforces the phase deadline

The two manifests (installed-evidence and final-source-integrity) share one cumulative 60 s preflight allowance (:239) with admission, source preflight and three validations. With 672 lock packages (lucide-react, date-fns, typescript among them), tens of thousands of entries are plausible. An overrun refuses with PHASE_DEADLINE_* and consumes the attempt, possibly after all tests have passed. Timing is NOT MEASURED.
upheld.fix: Throttle healthy() during manifest, for example every N entries or every 0.5 s, and record how long each manifest takes. Otherwise state explicitly in the decision that the 60 s bucket includes two full installed-tree hashes.

upheld.anchor: .github/workflows/quick-order-ci-pilot.yml:636,:808-827,:964@e86ffe39; WEBSITE_COMPLETION_EXPLICIT_DIRECT_AUTHORITY_20261011.txt ('Failure produces evidence and a specific correction/rerun decision')
upheld.title: An ordinary failure discards the in-limit evidence a correction decision needs (W2-10, raised from P3)
upheld.claim:
Any failure makes the payload metadata-only (:810). Its diagnostics are only top-level OUT/*.json files of 64 KiB or less (:824-826). That excludes the per-test Vitest JSON in OUT/<label>/<label>.json, which holds failureMessages, and the fully drained child streams, even when both are well within the 2/20 MiB limits. installed-integrity.json, with about 672 entries, is likely over 64 KiB as well. The raw files stay on the ephemeral runner, which is destroyed.

After a test failure, the single attempt therefore yields a reason code and an exit status but not which assertion failed. That falls short of the authority's requirement that failure produce evidence for a specific correction or rerun decision.

Two smaller defects:
- complete=outcome is None (:636) marks fully drained streams as incomplete.
- include-hidden-files: false (:964) could silently drop a dotfile that receipt.json lists.

Raised to P2 because the authority text, which neither lens cited, makes failure evidence a condition.
upheld.fix: For ordinary failures within limits, export the complete bounded OUT files. Keep metadata-only for overflow, unknown and symlink states. Derive stream completeness from EOF or drain state, not from success. Either set include-hidden-files: true or refuse when OUT contains hidden files.

upheld.title: Step timeouts add unselected ceilings below the controller allocations (W2-6)
upheld.claim:
The step timeouts sum to exactly 30 minutes.
- The 21-minute execution step (1260 s) is shorter than the 60 + 365 + 305 + 3x185 = 1285 s of allocations inside it.
- The 1-minute admission step equals the 60 s preflight allocation with no margin for work before and after the phase.

The outcome is fail-closed: a step timeout is not a cancellation, so collection still runs. However, SIGINT and then SIGTERM after 7.5 s can cut finish_container short.
upheld.fix: Set step timeouts as backstops at or above the controller allocations, keeping job timeout-minutes: 30 as the outer bound. Alternatively, name them in the decision text as additional selected ceilings.

upheld.title: A memory.events 'max' count above 0 refuses even when no OOM occurs (W2-7)
upheld.claim: In cgroup v2, the 'max' counter increments when usage reaches memory.max and the kernel reclaims, which includes page cache charged by npm ci writes. It does not mean an OOM happened. The adopted choice is a 2 GiB ceiling with OOM recording, so refusing on contact is stricter than adopted and consumes the attempt. The install footprint is NOT MEASURED. Raise this to P2 if a measured install approaches 2 GiB.
upheld.fix: Record 'max'. Refuse only on oom, oom_kill or OOMKilled. Alternatively, name refusal on contact with the cap in the decision text.

upheld.title: Isolation flags are not inspected after create, and the npm cache stays writable in test containers (W2-8)
upheld.claim: Post-create inspection checks memory, swap, PIDs, CPU, user and the read-only root. It does not check NetworkMode none for tests, CapDrop ALL, no-new-privileges, per-mount RO/RW, tmpfs or the log driver. /ci-cache is bind-mounted writable into all three test containers, although r2 lists only dependencies and output as writable for tests.
upheld.fix: Require the expected NetworkMode, CapDrop, SecurityOpt, per-mount RW flags, tmpfs and log driver after create. Omit the cache mount from test containers, or mount it read-only.

upheld.title: The worker heap check would pass even if 1024 MiB never took effect (W2-9)
upheld.claim: The check 0 < heap_size_limit < 1152 MiB also accepts a default heap sized from the cgroup, which is plausibly under 1024 MiB. Only the NODE_OPTIONS string comparison corroborates the selected value.
upheld.fix: Use heap_size_limit >= 1024 MiB as the lower bound and keep the 1152 MiB upper bound. A correct run is reasoned to be about 1048 MiB (NOT RUN).

upheld.title: Tight per-call docker CLI bounds and an undocumented anchored name filter (W2-11, cause corrected)
upheld.claim:
Each inspect, rm and ps call in finish_container is bounded at 0.5 s. The worst-case sum exceeds the 5 s grace. One slow CLI call on a passing run refuses. Per the bytes, the recorded first cause is CONTROL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT from small(), or TERMINATION_GRACE_EXPIRED from bounded(), not CONTAINER_CLEANUP_UNKNOWN.

The filter name=^/<name>$ relies on regex and leading-slash behaviour that docs.docker.com does not document. If the anchors are not honoured, a leftover is not inspected, and the label check at :781 refuses without its exit or OOM record.
upheld.fix: Find containers by label=xenios-ci-pilot=<RUN> and compare {{.Names}} for exact equality. Replace the fixed 0.5 s per-call bounds with a single remaining-grace budget.

upheld.title: child.exit is written non-atomically and read as soon as it exists (W2V-2)
upheld.claim: A shell redirect creates and truncates the file before writing it. If the host polls in that window it reads '', which refuses with CHILD_EXIT_RECEIPT on a passing test. The window is microseconds: low probability, fail-closed.
upheld.fix: Write child.exit.tmp and rename it into place, or treat an empty read as not yet present within the existing bound.

upheld.title: The BIND contract is untyped and partly procedural, and ACTIONS carries an unguarded placeholder (merges W1V-2, W1V-3, W2V-3)
upheld.claim:
Type requirements differ by field and are not recorded anywhere:
- actor_id must be a decimal string (:343 compares it with an environment string and runs re.fullmatch). The only recorded candidate is the JSON number 262137643; copied as an int it refuses with ACTOR_IMMUTABLE_ID.

The seven receipt-type fields are machine-checked only as not 'UNBOUND' and not None (:341), so '' or 'PENDING' would pass, while :84-86 and the handoff read as machine enforcement. ACTIONS['declared_runtime'] stays a placeholder outside the :341 guard and is written into actionPins (:327, :716).
upheld.fix: Record a typed binding schema for the successor, and have the successor comparison type-check every literal. Label the receipt fields as procedural, with substance verified only at comparison. Remove ACTIONS['declared_runtime'] or derive it from the observed manifests.

upheld.title: The ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG and ACTIONS_RUNNER_DEBUG='false' job env entries do not control anything (merges W1-7, W2-13)
upheld.claim: Per docs.github.com, debug logging is enabled through a repository secret or variable, or by a debug re-run. Job env entries are not documented as a control. The runner also echoes the inline controller and step env into the provider log; there are no secrets in them.
upheld.fix: Label these lines as non-controlling in the records. Add a pre-dispatch check that no such secret or variable exists. Keep provider-log control under the UNBOUND provider_action_log_control_receipt.

These unbound provider facts can each refuse and consume the attempt:

The records list none of them.
